key: In all their affliction He was afflicted, and the angel of His presence saved them; in His love and in His pity He redeemed them; And He bore them, and carried them all the days of old.
s: Recounting the LORD’s mercies to the house of Israel, whom He called children who would not deal falsely; Rashi, on 63:9, reads it as His not afflicting them as their deeds deserved, since Michael, prince of the Presence, always saved them, and Ibn Ezra, on 63:9, as His being distressed, as it were, and so hastening to save.

evidence.words: לא היצר להם כפי מעלליהם שהיו ראויין ללקות כי מלאך פניו הוא מיכאל שר הפנים ממשמשי' לפניו הושיעם תמיד בשליחותו של מקום … האמת שהוא בוי"ו, כטעם ותקצר נפשו (שופטים י' ט"ו), דרך משל להבין … בצרה על כן מהר להושיעם
evidence.gloss: [Rashi:] He did not bring distress on them according to their deeds, for which they deserved to suffer, for the angel of His presence, Michael, prince of the Presence, of those who minister before Him, always saved them as the agent of the Omnipresent. … [Ibn Ezra:] The truth is that it is with a vav (to Him), in the sense of ‘and His soul was grieved’ (Judges 10:16), a figure of speech to make it understood … [as though He too were] in distress; therefore He hastened to save them.

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, Isaiah 63:9, at [396,9]). Plain sense faithful to 63:7 to 8 (the LORD’s mercies to the house of Israel; ‘children that will not deal falsely’). Both readings are in the commentators’ own words at 63:9: Rashi glosses the lemma as He did not distress them according to their deeds, and names the angel as Michael, prince of the Presence, who always saved them; Ibn Ezra takes the word as with vav, a figure, as though He too were in distress and so hastened to save. They genuinely differ (not afflicted, afflicted) and the sentence names both without resolving. CHANGED: removed ‘following the written text’ from Rashi’s reading, since Rashi nowhere says he follows the ketiv (that is Radak’s observation and the proposer’s inference); and ‘His children who would not lie’ became ‘whom He called children who would not deal falsely’, closer to 63:8. entry-check ok on the corrected entry.
